question: To what four-generation royal ancestry does the opening verse trace the prophet Zephaniah, and during whose reign did he minister?
opt1: Son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hizkiah (Hezekiah), in the days of Josiah king of Judah
opt2: Son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, in the days of Manasseh king of Judah
opt3: Son of Shaphan, son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, son of Nathan, in the days of Amon king of Judah
opt4: Son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, son of Asaph, son of Heman, in the days of Jehoiakim king of Judah
correct: Son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hizkiah (Hezekiah), in the days of Josiah king of Judah
explanation: Zephaniah traces his genealogy back four generations to King Hezekiah and prophesied during the reign of Josiah. Zephaniah 1:1 (KJV) - "The word of the LORD which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah."

question: What comprehensive, universal de-creation judgment introduces the divine speech in Zephaniah 1:2-3?
opt1: Sending a global deluge of water to drown all living flesh and overthrowing the high mountains of the earth
opt2: Utterly consuming all things from off the land: man, beast, fowls of heaven, fishes of the sea, and stumbling blocks with the wicked
opt3: Commanding fire from heaven to consume all palaces from the river of Egypt unto the Euphrates
opt4: Drying up all oceans and springs, turning the habitable world into an uninhabited desert of salt and sulfur
correct: Utterly consuming all things from off the land: man, beast, fowls of heaven, fishes of the sea, and stumbling blocks with the wicked
explanation: The prophecy begins with a sweeping reversal of Genesis creation, consuming man, beast, birds, and fish. Zephaniah 1:2-3 (KJV) - "I will utterly consume all things from off the land, saith the LORD. I will consume man and beast; I will consume the fowls of the heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumbling blocks with the wicked: and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the LORD."

question: What specific forms of syncretistic idolatry in Jerusalem are targeted for extermination in Zephaniah 1:4-6?
opt1: The worshippers of Dagon in the valley of Hinnom, the sorcerers of Egypt, and priests sacrificing children to Chemosh
opt2: The makers of golden calves in Bethel, the diviners of Philistia, and elders weeping for Tammuz at the north gate
opt3: The remnant of Baal with Chemarim priests, stargazers on housetops, those who swear by the LORD and by Malcham, and those turned back
opt4: The prophets of Asherah in the groves of Carmel, astrologers of Babylon, and merchants selling idols in the temple
correct: The remnant of Baal with Chemarim priests, stargazers on housetops, those who swear by the LORD and by Malcham, and those turned back
explanation: God condemns Baal worship, idolatrous Chemarim priests, astral cults on housetops, and syncretism between Yahweh and Malcham (Molech). Zephaniah 1:4-6 (KJV) - "I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with the priests; And them that worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and them that worship and that swear by the LORD, and that swear by Malcham; And them that are turned back from the LORD; and those that have not sought the LORD, nor enquired for him."

question: With what solemn sacrificial metaphor does the prophet announce the approaching Day of the LORD, and who are singled out for punishment?
opt1: The LORD hath erected an altar of judgment; punishing the foreign mercenaries, false scribes, and rebellious high priests
opt2: The LORD hath blown the ram's horn; punishing the merchants of Tyre, chariot captains, and those who wear mourning sackcloth
opt3: The LORD hath poured out sacrificial wine; punishing the governors of Samaria, heathen ambassadors, and uncircumcised soldiers
opt4: The LORD hath prepared a sacrifice and bid His guests; punishing the princes, the king's children, and all clothed with strange apparel
correct: The LORD hath prepared a sacrifice and bid His guests; punishing the princes, the king's children, and all clothed with strange apparel
explanation: Judah herself becomes the sacrificial victim whose arrogant royal elite adopting pagan foreign fashions are judged. Zephaniah 1:7-8 (KJV) - "Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD: for the day of the LORD is at hand: for the LORD hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests. And it shall come to pass in the day of the LORD's sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king's children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel."

question: What superstitious practice and violent extortion are condemned in verse 9, and from what gates of Jerusalem will cries arise in that day?
opt1: Those that leap on the threshold and fill masters' houses with violence and deceit; with cries from the Fish Gate and howling from the Second
opt2: Those that bow before the threshold of Dagon; with wailing from the Valley Gate and crashing from the Water Gate
opt3: Those that swear false oaths upon the temple steps; with shouts from the Corner Gate and mourning from the Fountain Gate
opt4: Those that cast lots upon the doorposts of the poor; with groaning from the Horse Gate and weeping from the East Gate
correct: Those that leap on the threshold and fill masters' houses with violence and deceit; with cries from the Fish Gate and howling from the Second
explanation: Superstitious threshold-leapers filling palaces with extortion will face invasion cries from the Fish Gate and Mishneh (Second quarter). Zephaniah 1:9-10 (KJV) - "In the same day also will I punish all those that leap on the threshold, which fill their masters' houses with violence and deceit. And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and an howling from the second, and a great crashing from the hills."

question: What commercial district of Jerusalem is summoned to howl because its silver-bearing merchant populace is annihilated in Zephaniah 1:11?
opt1: Ophel (the royal quarter), for all the goldsmiths are carried away and palace treasurers slain
opt2: Maktesh (the mortar / bazaar district), for all the merchant people are cut down and silver bearers cut off
opt3: Millo (the citadel rampart), for all foreign bankers are imprisoned and tax collectors blinded
opt4: Siloam (the pool valley), for all the craftsmen are impoverished and trade caravans plundered
correct: Maktesh (the mortar / bazaar district), for all the merchant people are cut down and silver bearers cut off
explanation: Maktesh, the hollow market basin of Jerusalem where merchants weighed silver, faces total commercial extinction. Zephaniah 1:11 (KJV) - "Howl, ye inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the merchant people are cut down; all they that bear silver are cut off."

question: How will the LORD thoroughly inspect Jerusalem, and what cynical, practical atheism characterizes the complacent men settled on their lees?
opt1: Purging Jerusalem with firebrands, condemning skeptics who boast: "There is no God in heaven to judge the sons of men"
opt2: Measuring Jerusalem with an iron reed, overthrowing elders who claim: "Our strength hath built these walls, not the Almighty"
opt3: Searching Jerusalem with candles, punishing men settled on their lees who say in heart: "The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil"
opt4: Examining Jerusalem with blazing torches, striking down mockers who scoff: "Where is the promise of his coming?"
correct: Searching Jerusalem with candles, punishing men settled on their lees who say in heart: "The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil"
explanation: God conducts a candle-lit search for practical deists who stagnate like settled wine dregs, denying God's active moral governance. Zephaniah 1:12 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil."

question: What covenant curses of frustration will render the wealth and architecture of these complacent elites completely futile in Zephaniah 1:13?
opt1: Their silver will be melted by invading armies, their sons slain at the gate, and their daughters given as captives to Babylon
opt2: Their storehouses will be consumed by locusts, their wells poisoned with gall, and their fields overgrown with thorns
opt3: Their ivory beds will be broken in pieces, their jewels scattered in streets, and their royal garments worn by strangers
opt4: Goods shall become a booty, houses a desolation: they shall build houses but not inhabit them, and plant vineyards but not drink wine thereof
correct: Goods shall become a booty, houses a desolation: they shall build houses but not inhabit them, and plant vineyards but not drink wine thereof
explanation: The classic Deuteronomy 28 curses fall upon them: building without inhabiting, planting vineyards without drinking the wine. Zephaniah 1:13 (KJV) - "Therefore their goods shall become a booty, and their houses a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof."

question: With what solemn accumulation of descriptive terms does Zephaniah portray the terrible arrival of the Great Day of the LORD in verses 14-16?
opt1: A day of wrath, trouble, distress, wasteness, desolation, darkness, gloominess, clouds, thick darkness, and trumpet alarm against fenced cities
opt2: A day of unquenchable fire, boiling brimstone, falling stars, roaring seas, shattered mountains, and burning foundations of the earth
opt3: A day of heavenly horses, glittering swords, drawn bows, seven thunders, lightning arrows, and universal panic among kings
opt4: A day of weeping, gnashing of teeth, famine, pestilence, silent sanctuaries, broken crowns, and dry rivers across all lands
correct: A day of wrath, trouble, distress, wasteness, desolation, darkness, gloominess, clouds, thick darkness, and trumpet alarm against fenced cities
explanation: This historic passage provided the biblical imagery for the Latin hymn 'Dies Irae', describing intense gloom, wrath, and battle alarms. Zephaniah 1:14-16 (KJV) - "The great day of the LORD is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the LORD: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness, A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities, and against the high towers."

question: What will be the total helplessness of human wealth and physical degradation of sinners in the day of the LORD's jealousy in Zephaniah 1:17-18?
opt1: Men shall hide in mountain caverns, their crowns trodden like clay, and all their silver vessels shall be melted into arrows of judgment
opt2: Men shall walk like blind men, blood poured as dust, flesh as dung; neither silver nor gold shall deliver them, and the land is devoured by fire
opt3: Men shall weep like motherless children, their strength dried up like potsherds, and their gold shall become a trap for foreign mercenaries
opt4: Men shall stumble into pit traps, their bones left unburied in fields, and their treasures shall be carried into the temple of Bel
correct: Men shall walk like blind men, blood poured as dust, flesh as dung; neither silver nor gold shall deliver them, and the land is devoured by fire
explanation: Sinners will wander blindly, their blood treated like worthless dust, unable to ransom their lives with silver or gold. Zephaniah 1:17-18 (KJV) - "And I will bring distress upon men, that they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the LORD: and their blood shall be poured out as dust, and their flesh as the dung. Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land."

question: What urgent summons to assemble in repentance is issued to the shameless nation before the decree brings forth in Zephaniah 2:1-2?
opt1: "Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly; before the lion cometh up from his thicket"
opt2: "Sanctify yourselves, put off your ornaments of gold, and weep between the porch and altar; before the fire consumeth the gate"
opt3: "Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff"
opt4: "Turn ye unto me with all your heart, and rend your garments; before the sun goeth down over the prophets of Jerusalem"
correct: "Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff"
explanation: Judah is summoned to assemble in repentance before judgment sweeps through like blown chaff. Zephaniah 2:1-2 (KJV) - "Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the LORD come upon you, before the day of the LORD's anger come upon you."

question: To whom is the path of divine refuge specifically directed in Zephaniah 2:3, and what must they seek in order to be hidden in the day of anger?
opt1: "Seek ye the priests of Levi, all ye princes of Judah; offer rams without blemish: peradventure the angel of death shall pass over"
opt2: "Seek ye the counsel of the king, all ye warriors of Zion; strengthen the battlements: it may be your iron shields will protect you"
opt3: "Seek ye the ancient paths of David, all ye elders of Israel; fast forty days in the wilderness: peradventure God will turn away His wrath"
opt4: "Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD's anger"
correct: "Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD's anger"
explanation: Refuge is promised not to the proud, but to the humble and meek who seek righteousness and obedience. Zephaniah 2:3 (KJV) - "Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD's anger."

question: What catastrophic fate is pronounced against the four major cities of Philistia and the nation of the Cherethites in Zephaniah 2:4-5?
opt1: Gaza forsaken, Ashkelon a desolation, Ashdod driven out at noonday, Ekron rooted up, and the Cherethite coast destroyed without inhabitant
opt2: Gath burned with fire, Gaza besieged with iron rams, Ashkelon submerged by waves, and Ekron's gods melted into silver dross
opt3: Ashdod poisoned by bitter waters, Gaza's walls broken by Babylon, Ekron sold into captivity, and Ashkelon's palaces laid waste
opt4: Gaza cast into the sea, Ashkelon given to desert wolves, Ashdod plowed like a field, and Ekron's inhabitants carried to Nineveh
correct: Gaza forsaken, Ashkelon a desolation, Ashdod driven out at noonday, Ekron rooted up, and the Cherethite coast destroyed without inhabitant
explanation: Judgment strikes Philistia's pentapolis (Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron) and the Cherethite seacoast. Zephaniah 2:4-5 (KJV) - "For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up. Woe unto the inhabitants of the sea coast, the nation of the Cherethites! the word of the LORD is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant."

question: Into what pastoral sanctuary will the devastated Philistine sea coast be transformed, and who will possess it in Zephaniah 2:6-7?
opt1: Vineyards of sweet wine and olive terraces, inherited by foreign merchant princes who pay annual tribute to Jerusalem
opt2: Cottages for shepherds and folds for flocks, becoming the heritage of the remnant of Judah who shall feed and lie down in Ashkelon
opt3: An uninhabited wilderness of thorn hedges and saltpits, avoided by all travelers traveling between Egypt and Tyre
opt4: Fortified naval harbors of iron, garrisoned by the sons of Benjamin to control maritime trade routes
correct: Cottages for shepherds and folds for flocks, becoming the heritage of the remnant of Judah who shall feed and lie down in Ashkelon
explanation: The militarized Philistine coast becomes peaceful pastureland for the restored remnant of Judah. Zephaniah 2:6-7 (KJV) - "And the sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks. And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: in the houses of Ashkelon shall they lie down in the evening: for the LORD their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity."

question: What devastating ancient judgment is promised upon Moab and Ammon for reproaching God's people and magnifying themselves against their border?
opt1: Moab shall be drowned in an overflowing flood, and Ammon burned like the high places of Tophet by foreign archers
opt2: Moab shall be divided among desert Bedouins, and Ammon's royal dynasty blinded and led in chains to Babylon
opt3: Moab shall be as Sodom, and Ammon as Gomorrah, a breeding of nettles, saltpits, and perpetual desolation spoiled by God's remnant
opt4: Moab shall become a swamp of bitter reeds, and Ammon's fortified citadels torn down stone by stone
correct: Moab shall be as Sodom, and Ammon as Gomorrah, a breeding of nettles, saltpits, and perpetual desolation spoiled by God's remnant
explanation: Because of their pride and insults against Judah, Moab and Ammon are sentenced to become like Sodom and Gomorrah. Zephaniah 2:8-10 (KJV) - "I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. Therefore as I live, saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD of hosts."

question: What striking theological phrase describes how the LORD will dismantle all pagan pantheons, leading to global monotheistic worship in Zephaniah 2:11?
opt1: "He will shatter all carved idols with lightning; and kings shall bring gold to His sanctuary in Jerusalem"
opt2: "He will melt all silver images in the furnace; and every knee shall bow upon the holy mountain of Zion"
opt3: "He will overthrow the altars of the Gentiles; and foreign priests shall renounce their vain incantations forever"
opt4: "He will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen"
correct: "He will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen"
explanation: Yahweh starves pagan gods of sacrificial nourishment, causing distant maritime nations to worship Him worldwide. Zephaniah 2:11 (KJV) - "The LORD will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen."

question: What judgments does the LORD pronounce against the southern power (Ethiopia/Cush) and the northern imperial oppressor (Assyria)?
opt1: Ethiopians shall be slain by His sword, and He will destroy Assyria, making Nineveh a desolation and dry like a wilderness
opt2: Ethiopians shall be sold as slaves to Tarshish, and Assyria shall be consumed by an overflowing river of fire
opt3: Ethiopians shall pay tribute in ivory, and Nineveh's palaces shall be overthrown by an earthquake at midnight
opt4: Ethiopians shall wander blind in the desert, and Assyrian princes shall be cast into the fiery furnace of Babylon
correct: Ethiopians shall be slain by His sword, and He will destroy Assyria, making Nineveh a desolation and dry like a wilderness
explanation: Judgment extends south to Ethiopia (slain by God's sword) and north to Assyria (Nineveh made arid like a wilderness). Zephaniah 2:12-13 (KJV) - "Ye Ethiopians also, ye shall be slain by my sword. And he will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness."

question: What wild beasts and birds will inhabit the ruined architectural lintels and exposed cedarwork of Nineveh in Zephaniah 2:14?
opt1: Desert jackals and horned owls dwelling in royal bedchambers, serpents nesting under marble steps, and foxes roaming the walls
opt2: Flocks and beasts of nations lying down, cormorant and bittern lodging in upper lintels, singing in windows, with cedarwork uncovered
opt3: Lions and young whelps walking through golden banquet halls, ravens croaking upon bronze doors, and scorpions filling the floor
opt4: Ostriches and wild wolves crying in the palaces of ivory, vultures perching upon shattered ramparts, and weeds choking the gates
correct: Flocks and beasts of nations lying down, cormorant and bittern lodging in upper lintels, singing in windows, with cedarwork uncovered
explanation: Nineveh's magnificent cedar-paneled architecture becomes an eerie habitat for wild desert birds and resting flocks. Zephaniah 2:14 (KJV) - "And flocks shall lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts of the nations: both the cormorant and the bittern shall lodge in the upper lintels of it; their voice shall sing in the windows; desolation shall be in the thresholds: for he shall uncover the cedar work."

question: With what arrogant blasphemy did Nineveh boast in her former security, and what reaction will passers-by display over her ruin in Zephaniah 2:15?
opt1: She boasted, "My walls touch the heavens and my river cannot dry"; yet passers-by shall weep and cast dust on their heads in pity
opt2: She claimed, "No king on earth can conquer my chariots"; yet passers-by shall plunder her bronze weapons with great shouting
opt3: She said in her heart, "I am, and there is none beside me"; yet became a desolation for beasts, where every passer-by shall hiss and wag his hand
opt4: She declared, "I sit a queen forever and shall see no sorrow"; yet passers-by shall shudder and flee from her pestilence
correct: She said in her heart, "I am, and there is none beside me"; yet became a desolation for beasts, where every passer-by shall hiss and wag his hand
explanation: Nineveh usurped divine language ('I am, and there is none beside me'), only to become a mocked ruin where passers-by hiss and wag hands. Zephaniah 2:15 (KJV) - "This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in! every one that passeth by her shall hiss, and wag his hand."

question: Across what complete geographical compass does the prophetic judgment of Chapter 2 sweep to demonstrate the universal reign of Yahweh?
opt1: North (Syria and Damascus), South (Egypt and Midian), East (Persia and Media), and West (Cyprus and Greece)
opt2: East (Babylon and Chaldea), West (Phoenicia and Tyre), North (Urartu and Scythia), and South (Arabia and Sheba)
opt3: South (Edom and Seir), North (Lebanon and Sidon), West (the Mediterranean isles), and East (Mesopotamia)
opt4: West (Philistia), East (Moab and Ammon), South (Ethiopia/Cush), and North (Assyria and Nineveh)
correct: West (Philistia), East (Moab and Ammon), South (Ethiopia/Cush), and North (Assyria and Nineveh)
explanation: Chapter 2 systematically surveys the four compass points surrounding Judah: West (Philistia), East (Moab/Ammon), South (Cush), and North (Assyria). Zephaniah 2:4-15 (KJV) - "For Gaza shall be forsaken ... Surely Moab shall be as Sodom ... Ye Ethiopians also ... And he will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria ... "

question: With what fourfold spiritual indictment does the prophet pronounce woe against the filthy, polluted, and oppressing city of Jerusalem in Zephaniah 3:2?
opt1: "She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she trusted not in the LORD; she drew not near to her God"
opt2: "She kept not the Sabbath; she offered not clean sacrifices; she remembered not the covenant; she walked not in His statutes"
opt3: "She listened to false diviners; she shed the blood of the righteous; she turned away from wisdom; she broke the holy law"
opt4: "She built high places to Baal; she loved the hire of an harlot; she despised the prophets; she forsook the sanctuary"
correct: "She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she trusted not in the LORD; she drew not near to her God"
explanation: Jerusalem's core spiritual rebellion is summarized in four negative clauses of disobedience, pride, distrust, and distance from God. Zephaniah 3:1-2 (KJV) - "Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city! She obeyed not the voice; she received not correction; she trusted not in the LORD; she drew not near to her God."

question: What animal and behavioral metaphors characterize the four governing leadership classes of Jerusalem in Zephaniah 3:3-4?
opt1: Princes are ravenous leopards, judges are deaf adders, prophets are greedy dogs, and priests offer blind sacrifices
opt2: Princes are roaring lions, judges are evening wolves gnawing not bones till morrow, prophets are treacherous, and priests violate the law
opt3: Princes are wild bulls of Bashan, judges are pitiless bears, prophets are smooth deceivers, and priests drink wine in the temple
opt4: Princes are oppressive taskmasters, judges are corrupt merchants, prophets are hirelings, and priests worship host of heaven
correct: Princes are roaring lions, judges are evening wolves gnawing not bones till morrow, prophets are treacherous, and priests violate the law
explanation: The civil rulers act like rapacious predators (lions and wolves), while religious leaders are fickle, treacherous, and profane holy things. Zephaniah 3:3-4 (KJV) - "Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves; they gnaw not the bones till the morrow. Her prophets are light and treacherous persons: her priests have polluted the sanctuary, they have done violence to the law."

question: In striking contrast to Jerusalem's shameful corrupt leaders, how is the character and daily justice of the LORD portrayed in Zephaniah 3:5?
opt1: The holy God sitteth upon His throne in heaven, executing vengeance by midnight lightning, while sinners tremble in dust
opt2: The righteous King waiteth with long-suffering patience, offering forgiveness to all who weep, while the wicked mock His mercy
opt3: The just LORD is in her midst doing no iniquity, bringing His judgment to light every morning without failing, while the unjust knows no shame
opt4: The eternal Judge weigheth all souls in righteous balances, revealing His glory at sunset, while priests hide their eyes in fear
correct: The just LORD is in her midst doing no iniquity, bringing His judgment to light every morning without failing, while the unjust knows no shame
explanation: God's unchanging morning-by-morning justice in the very midst of Jerusalem highlights the shamelessness of her unjust leaders. Zephaniah 3:5 (KJV) - "The just LORD is in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity: every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he faileth not; but the unjust knoweth no shame."

question: Despite God's warnings through destroyed nations, how did Jerusalem respond, leading to what divine resolution to devour the earth in Zephaniah 3:7-8?
opt1: They rent their garments in pretense and multiplied idolatry; leading God to send seven plagues of locusts to strip the land
opt2: They mocked the prophets and formed an alliance with Egypt; leading God to deliver the city into the hands of Sennacherib
opt3: They offered stolen goods upon the altar; leading God to seal the gates of heaven and withhold rain for three full years
opt4: They rose early and corrupted all their doings; leading God to assemble nations to pour His indignation and devour all earth with fire of jealousy
correct: They rose early and corrupted all their doings; leading God to assemble nations to pour His indignation and devour all earth with fire of jealousy
explanation: Judah eagerly redoubled corruption ('rose early and corrupted'), provoking God's determination to assemble nations and devour the earth with His jealous fire. Zephaniah 3:7-8 (KJV) - "I said, Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive instruction; so their dwelling should not be cut off, howsoever I punished them: but they rose early, and corrupted all their doings. Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the LORD, until the day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them mine indignation, even all my fierce anger: for all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy."

question: What glorious global transformation and unified worship will the LORD bestow upon the nations in Zephaniah 3:9-10?
opt1: A pure language to call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him with one consent, with suppliants beyond Ethiopia bringing offerings
opt2: A heavenly scroll written in gold letters to teach the fear of God, with kings from the ends of the earth building altars in Jerusalem
opt3: A universal peace covenant ending all war, with ambassadors from all islands presenting incense and purple fabrics to the King
opt4: A great awakening of prophetic visions among young and old, with Gentile priests offering clean bullocks upon Mount Zion
correct: A pure language to call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him with one consent, with suppliants beyond Ethiopia bringing offerings
explanation: Reversing Babel, God gives the nations a purified lip/language to call upon Yahweh with one shoulder (one consent). Zephaniah 3:9-10 (KJV) - "For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one consent. From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering."

question: Whom will the LORD remove from Jerusalem, and what will be the spiritual character and peaceful state of the remnant left in her midst in Zephaniah 3:12-13?
opt1: The uncircumcised expelled, leaving wealthy princes who rebuild the temple, offering daily sacrifices and singing psalms of David
opt2: The haughty removed, leaving an afflicted and poor people who trust in the LORD, doing no iniquity, speaking no lies, and feeding without fear
opt3: The foreign merchants banished, leaving mighty warriors who defend the walls of Zion and conquer neighboring heathen kingdoms
opt4: The rebellious elders executed, leaving Nazirites who fast continuously, wear white linen, and guard the Ark of the Covenant
correct: The haughty removed, leaving an afflicted and poor people who trust in the LORD, doing no iniquity, speaking no lies, and feeding without fear
explanation: God purges religious arrogance, establishing a humble, truthful, and secure remnant who trust wholly in Yahweh's name. Zephaniah 3:11-13 (KJV) - "In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain. I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the LORD. The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid."

question: What jubilant victory anthem is daughter Zion commanded to sing, and why will she fear evil no more in Zephaniah 3:14-15?

question: In one of the most tender revelations of divine affection in Scripture, how does the LORD express His saving love and joy over His redeemed people in Zephaniah 3:17?

question: Whom will the LORD gather and vindicate, reversing their historical disgrace into worldwide renown in Zephaniah 3:18-19?
opt1: Those sorrowful for the solemn assembly, saving her that halteth, gathering the driven out, giving them praise and fame where they suffered shame

opt3: The children of the kings of Judah, crowning them upon the throne of David and granting them victory over all the armies of the Gentiles

correct: Those sorrowful for the solemn assembly, saving her that halteth, gathering the driven out, giving them praise and fame where they suffered shame
explanation: God tenderly restores the disenfranchised, the sorrowful mourners of the festivals, and the halting outcasts, exchanging their shame for praise. Zephaniah 3:18-19 (KJV) - "I will gather them that are sorrowful for the solemn assembly, who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden. Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out; and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame."

question: With what definitive promise of covenant restoration and international praise does the Book of Zephaniah conclude in verse 20?

explanation: The prophecy closes with God's personal pledge to gather His exiles, overturn their captivity, and establish them as a name and praise worldwide. Zephaniah 3:20 (KJV) - "At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the LORD."
